head:
Executive Ohrt
To enable the employees in the Government service to participate in the
ceremonies incident to the dedication of the Memorial to General Ulysses S.
Grant, late President of the United States, on the One Hundredth Anniversary
of his birth, April 27, 1922, it is hereby ordered that on that date four hours,
exclusive of time for luncheon, shall constitute a day's work for all clerks and
other employees, including per diem employees, of the Federal Government, and
the Government of the District of Columbia, in the said District of Columbia.
Provided, however, that this order shall not apply to any bureau or office
of the Federal Government, or the District of Columbia, or to any of the
clerks or per diem employees thereof, that may for special public reasons be
excepted therefrom by the head of the Department having supervision or
control of such bureau or office, or where the same would be inconsistent with
the provisions of existing law.
WARREN G HARDING
THE WHITE House,
April 2,5, 1922.
[No. 3665.]

By virtue of the authority vested in me by an Act of Congress entitled
"An act to define, regulate, and punish trading with the enemy and for other
Purposes", approved October 6th, 191, known as the "Trading with the Enemy
Act" and the Amendment to such Act embodied in "An act making appropria-
tions to supply urgent deficiencies in the appropriations for the fiscal year
ending June 30, 191i8, and prior fiscal years on account of war expenses and for
other Purposes," approved March 28, 1918, and the Amendment to such Act
embodied in "An act making appropriations to supply deficiencies in appro-
priations for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1919, and prior fiscal years on
account of war expenses, and for other Purposes", approved November 4, 1918,
to make certain orders such as that herein contained, I hereby, in the public
interest, make the following determination, order, rule and regulation:
The Ale ryu odian is hereby authorized to sell at private sale,
at such time and place as to him or to his authorized agent may seem advisable,
without public or other advertisement, certain real estate now being held and
administered by him as such Alien Property Custodian, and heretofore, upon
requirement, conveyed, transferred, assigned and delivered to him as the
property of "the widow and heirs-at-law and next of kin of Edward Schmitt,
deceased, names unknown, whose address

north, Range fourteen (14), East of the 3rd P. M, as recorded in Book 2722,
Page 189, Recorder's Office, Cook County, Illinois, with the improvements
thereon.
My reasons for the foregoing determination, order, rule and regulation are:
(a) That property such as that herein described can not usually be sold to
advantage at public sale after public or other advertisement.

received by the Alien Property Custodian.

be avoided.

By virture of the authority vested in me, the Executive Order of December 3""-~
1921, prescribing the basis for making charges against employees of The Panama
Canal and Panama Railroad on the Isthmus of Panama for rent, fuel, electric
current, water, and services in connection with the use of quarters, on and after

prescribe a lower rate of charges for official and other quarters which officers
and employees of The Panama Canal and Panama Railroad Company are re-
quired to occupy by reason of the office held or the duties performed by them,

Schedule A, Subdivision III, Paragraph 13, of positions excepted from the
requirement of examinations under Schedule A of the Civil Service Rules is
hereby amended to read as follows:
13. All persons actually employed in leprosy investigation stations.
This amendment, which is requested by the Treasury Department and
concurred in by the Civil Service Commission makes general the exception from
examination' which formerly applied only to the leprosy investigation station
at Ntolokai, Hawaii. It is based upon the fact that it is impracticable to fill the
positions in the usual manner through competitive examination because of the
class of patients treated.
